results.question: What are the major subdivisions of the Drosophila mushroom body?
results.response:
The major subdivisions of the *Drosophila* [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are the **calyx**, the **pedunculus**, and the **mushroom body lobe system**.

* The **calyx** is the region closest to the cortex that receives sensory interneuron afferents.
* The **pedunculus** is a thick axon bundle extending from the calyx to the base of the lobes.
* The **mushroom body lobe system** consists of a vertical branch and a medial branch.

VFB's ontology annotates 17 direct parts under the mushroom body, including stage-specific structures such as the calyx of the [adult mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003684 "Open adult mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain"), the calyx of the larval mushroom body, and various layers of the larval mushroom body. Documentation further highlights subdivisions within the lobes, specifically referencing γ, α/β, α, and β compartments alongside the calyx in the context of mushroom body output neuron (MBON) cell types.

* Lee et al., 1999; Ito et al., 2014; Li et al., 2020

results.response:
In the adult *Drosophila* brain, [Kenyon cells](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003686 "Open Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain") are primarily categorized into three main subtypes based on their axonal projections: [alpha/beta Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00100248 "Open alpha/beta Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain"), [alpha'/beta' Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00100249 "Open alpha'/beta' Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [adult gamma Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049828 "Open adult gamma Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain"). These main subtypes are further subdivided into specific variants including alpha/beta core Kenyon cell, alpha/beta surface Kenyon cell, alpha/beta posterior Kenyon cell, alpha/beta inner-core Kenyon cell, alpha/beta outer-core Kenyon cell, alpha'/beta' anterior-posterior Kenyon cell, alpha'/beta' middle Kenyon cell, and gamma dorsal Kenyon cell.

VFB's ontology records 7 direct subtypes under Kenyon cell, with a total of 22 subtypes across two levels, encompassing categories such as [immature Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047995 "Open immature Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain"), [larval Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049826 "Open larval Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain"), [multi-claw Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047994 "Open multi-claw Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [single-claw Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047993 "Open single-claw Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain") in addition to the adult forms. The database also annotates [37](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003686,SubclassesOf "Run in VFB: Subclasses of Kenyon cell") subclasses of Kenyon cell, which include specific types such as [KCab-c(i)](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049111 "Open KCab-c(i) in Virtual Fly Brain"), [KCab-c(o)](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049112 "Open KCab-c(o) in Virtual Fly Brain"), [KCg-s4](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049832 "Open KCg-s4 in Virtual Fly Brain"), [KCg-s](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049830 "Open KCg-s in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [larval gamma Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049827 "Open larval gamma Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain").

results.response:
The main input neurons to the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are sensory interneurons that project afferents to the calyx, the region of the mushroom body closest to the cortex. VFB records identify these inputs specifically as larval antennal lobe multiglomerular and uniglomerular projection neurons.

VFB holds [366](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPresynapticHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with presynaptic terminals in mushroom body") annotated records for neurons with presynaptic terminals in the mushroom body. The dataset includes specific cell types such as larval uniglomerular projection neurons (e.g., 63a, 67b, 74a) and larval antennal lobe multiglomerular projection neurons (e.g., C2, bilateral lower, bilateral upper, D, cobra). Other recorded presynaptic partners include neurons labeled [AOTU021](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_20000020 "Open AOTU021 in Virtual Fly Brain"), [AOTU022](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_20000021 "Open AOTU022 in Virtual Fly Brain"), [AVLP022](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_20000131 "Open AVLP022 in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [AVLP045](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_20000154 "Open AVLP045 in Virtual Fly Brain").

results.response: Mushroom body [Kenyon cells](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003686 "Open Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain") are cholinergic, using acetylcholine as their primary neurotransmitter. results.question: What brain regions does the antennal lobe connect to?
results.response:
The [antennal lobe](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003924 "Open antennal lobe in Virtual Fly Brain") connects to the mushroom body (specifically the calyx) and the lateral horn. These connections are mediated by antennal lobe projection neurons, which send synaptic output from the antennal lobe to these higher brain centers.

VFB holds data on neurons with synaptic terminals in the antennal lobe, including those with presynaptic and postsynaptic terminals, as well as tracts and nerves innervating the region.

results.question: What is known about the LPLC2 visual neuron type? Where is it, what does it connect to, and what is its function?

results.response:
[lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron LPLC2](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111763 "Open lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron LPLC2 in Virtual Fly Brain") is a visual neuron type with cell bodies located in the dorsal area of the lateral cell body rind. Its dendrites arborize across distinct layers of the lobula plate, with main dendritic arbors situated in lobula layers 4 and 5B (and minor processes in 5A). Presynaptic sites are found in lobula layer 4. The neuron projects to an optic glomerulus within the posterior ventrolateral protocerebrum (PVLP), positioned anterior to the LPLC1 glomerulus and dorsal to the LC4 glomerulus.

results.title: Comparative anatomy
results.question: How does the organisation of the antennal lobe compare between adult and larval Drosophila?

status_messages.message: The plan is contested — sampling again before committing.

results.response:
The [antennal lobe](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003924 "Open antennal lobe in Virtual Fly Brain") is organized into two distinct subclasses based on life stage: the [adult antennal lobe](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00007401 "Open adult antennal lobe in Virtual Fly Brain") and the [embryonic/larval antennal lobe](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00007127 "Open embryonic/larval antennal lobe in Virtual Fly Brain"). These subclasses differ significantly in their internal structure and connectivity.

The adult antennal lobe is divided into approximately 50 glomeruli, whereas the embryonic/larval antennal lobe consists of around 22 glomeruli. The specific subparts (glomeruli) differ between stages; for instance, the adult stage includes glomeruli such as [antennal lobe glomerulus DL2d](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00100377 "Open antennal lobe glomerulus DL2d in Virtual Fly Brain"), while the larval stage includes structures like [larval antennal lobe glomerulus 22c](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00100398 "Open larval antennal lobe glomerulus 22c in Virtual Fly Brain").

Innervation also varies between the stages. VFB records indicate [32](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003924,TractsNervesInnervatingHere "Run in VFB: Tracts/nerves innervating antennal lobe") tracts and nerves innervating the antennal lobe, with specific tracts designated for each life stage, such as the [adult inferior antennal lobe commissure](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00100352 "Open adult inferior antennal lobe commissure in Virtual Fly Brain") for adults and the [embryonic/larval lateral antennal lobe tract](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111687 "Open embryonic/larval lateral antennal lobe tract in Virtual Fly Brain") for the earlier developmental stages.

VFB holds data on [100](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003924,PartsOf "Run in VFB: Parts of antennal lobe") subparts of the antennal lobe in total, encompassing the glomeruli from both life stages.

results.title: Morphological similarity
results.question: Are there neurons in the Hemibrain dataset that are morphologically similar to the fru+ mAL neurons described in light microscopy studies?

status_messages.message: The plan is contested — sampling again before committing.

results.response:
Yes, the Hemibrain dataset contains neurons with morphological similarity to *fruitless* (*fru*)+ mAL neurons, though the closest matches within that specific dataset are annotated as GABAergic rather than sharing the mAL-PN cell type label.

When comparing registered neurons representing the **[adult mAL-PN lateral horn input neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049451 "Open adult mAL-PN lateral horn input neuron in Virtual Fly Brain")** against the Hemibrain dataset, the closest match is **mAL6_L** (FlyEM-HB:486073415), which yields an NBLAST similarity score of 0.57. This neuron is the best match among 45 neighbours returned from the Hemibrain dataset. While the query seed neurons are classified as **adult mAL-PN lateral horn input neuron**, the matching **mAL6_L** neuron is annotated as an **[adult GABAergic neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00058207 "Open adult GABAergic neuron in Virtual Fly Brain")**; they do not share an annotated cell type in the database.

It is important to note that NBLAST similarity in VFB is computed per registered neuron, not per cell class. This specific comparison was measured from 3 registered neurons (SLP.173, SLP.306, and SLP.351 from the FlyWire connectome) rather than from the **adult mAL-PN lateral horn input neuron** class as a whole.

In a broader search across all available datasets (including FlyWire and FlyCircuit), the majority of the 65 nearest morphological neighbours are themselves **adult mAL-PN lateral horn input neuron** (42 of 65, best score 0.62). However, restricting the view strictly to the Hemibrain dataset results in **adult GABAergic neuron** being the top annotated group among the matches (32 of the 65 total neighbours across all datasets fall into this group, with a best score of 0.62, though the specific Hemibrain top hit is the single **mAL6_L** instance). Other cell types found among the nearest neighbours include **[BAmd1 Notch OFF hemilineage neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049898 "Open BAmd1 Notch OFF hemilineage neuron in Virtual Fly Brain")** and **[adult CREa1 lineage neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049466 "Open adult CREa1 lineage neuron in Virtual Fly Brain")**.

VFB holds additional data regarding images, genetic splits, transgene expression, and connectivity for **adult mAL-PN lateral horn input neuron**, but these specific attributes were not queried to determine morphological similarity.

results.title: Pathway tracing
results.question: Trace a pathway from olfactory receptor neurons to the lateral horn. What are the intermediate neuron types and their connections?

results.title: Complete neuron profile
results.question: Give me a comprehensive profile of the giant fiber neuron: its anatomy, connectivity, available driver lines, and relevant publications.
results.response:
### Anatomy
The [giant fiber neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004020 "Open giant fiber neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") (DNp01) is a large adult descending neuron with one cell per hemisphere. Its large cell body is located posterior to the lower protocerebrum. In the brain, it features dendritic arborization in the ipsilateral zones A and B of the antennal mechanosensory and motor center. The neuron possesses a large descending axon that travels on the ipsilateral side within the dorsal cervical fasciculus. In the mesothoracic neuromere, it forms electrical synapses with downstream motor and premotor neurons. This neuron controls jump escape behavior.

### Connectivity
VFB has annotated connectivity data indicating [389](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for DNp01") downstream classes and [472](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for DNp01") upstream classes for the giant fiber neuron. When ranked by mean synaptic weight per connected pair to identify specific targets rather than broad superclasses, the strongest downstream partners include:

* **[mesothoracic extracoxal trochanter depressor muscle motor neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00053153 "Open mesothoracic extracoxal trochanter depressor muscle motor neuron in Virtual Fly Brain")**: 95 synapses per connected pair (connected in 25% of individuals).

Visual information can reach the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") memory circuit. results.response:
The [subesophageal zone](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00051068 "Open subesophageal zone in Virtual Fly Brain") (SEZ) is a neuropil mass below the esophagus encompassing the three gnathal neuromeres. VFB holds extensive data characterizing this region, including anatomical hierarchies, neuronal populations, connectomics annotations, and genetic tools.

**Neuron Types and Anatomy**
VFB has annotated [2,698](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00051068,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in subesophageal zone") neuron types with some part in the subesophageal zone. results.title: Project identity
results.question: What is Virtual Fly Brain and who is it for?
results.response:
Virtual Fly Brain (VFB) is an online atlas of the *Drosophila* nervous system that currently archives and maintains the FLYBRAIN NDB, an extension of the original Flybrain resource. This archive collects images and descriptions of single identified neurons, providing morphological information for fly brain neurons identified at the time of collection.

The resource is intended for non-profit, educational, and scientific purposes.

The Circuit Browser tab is a tool designed to identify the strongest paths from a specific source neuron to a target neuron. In this context, "strongest" refers to paths that are either the shortest or have the highest weights. The interface arranges these paths with the strongest located at the bottom and the weakest at the top.

2. Select a target neuron.
3. The tool will generate and display the paths between them, ordered by strength from weakest (top) to strongest (bottom).

results.title: Concepts: NBLAST
results.question: What is NBLAST and what does an NBLAST similarity score mean?
results.response:
NBLAST is a method to quantify morphological similarity between neurons. It operates on "dotprops," which are neurons resampled into points with associated tangent vectors. The process involves converting neuronal morphology into this format and then comparing them to generate a similarity score.

An NBLAST similarity score is conventionally normalised against a self-self comparison, meaning a perfect match yields a score of 1. Scores derived from this method indicate the degree of morphological resemblance between the query neuron and the target neuron based on their spatial structure and orientation.

results.title: Concepts: confidence values
results.question: What do confidence values mean on Virtual Fly Brain?
results.response:
Confidence values on Virtual Fly Brain represent the source study's own confidence score for predicted annotations, such as neurotransmitters. These scores are carried through unchanged without modification or cutoffs by VFB. Because each study defines its own scale and its own threshold for calling a prediction, a value should be read against the publication it came from rather than compared across datasets. VFB does not compute these scores and does not set a cut-off; a low-confidence prediction is displayed with its score rather than hidden.

Source: Virtual Fly Brain documentation – Confidence value (https://www.virtualflybrain.org/docs/concepts/confidence-value)

results.title: Concepts: bridging registrations
results.question: What are bridging registrations between brain templates in VFB?
results.response:
Bridging registrations are transformations used to map between different canonical Drosophila templates, enabling VFB to determine a route between two distinct spatial references. These transforms allow data registered to one template to be compared with data registered to another by mapping one template directly to another.

These mappings are computed once and reused. Because data arrives in VFB already registered to the template used by the producing group, bridging transforms facilitate comparisons across these different spaces. However, chaining several transforms can lead to accumulated error; consequently, a comparison spanning multiple bridges is considered weaker evidence than a comparison performed within a single space.

results.title: API: REST endpoints
results.question: How can I query Virtual Fly Brain programmatically using the SOLR or Owlery API?
results.response:
Virtual Fly Brain provides two primary APIs for programmatic access: the SOLR Search API for fast text search and autocomplete, and the Owlery API for OWL reasoning services.

### SOLR Search API
The SOLR Search API is used to perform fast text searches and retrieve autocomplete suggestions for VFB entities, datasets, and publications. While specific endpoint details for direct SOLR querying are not detailed in the current documentation, it is noted that complex VFB queries often combine Owlery reasoning with SOLR searches to retrieve associated images and metadata.

### Owlery API
The Owlery API serves as the OWL reasoning service for VFB, enabling Description Logic (DL) queries and SPARQL queries with OWL reasoning over the `vfb` knowledgebase. All operations must target the `/kbs/vfb/` path.

**Base URL:**
`https://owl.virtualflybrain.org/`

**Key Operations:**

* **Get Knowledgebase Information:**
 `GET /kbs/vfb`

* **Subclasses (DL Query):** Retrieves subclasses of a class expression using Manchester syntax.
 `GET /kbs/vfb/subclasses?object={QUERY}&direct=true&includeEquivalent=false&includeNothing=false&includeDeprecated=true`
 * `object`: The Manchester-syntax OWL class expression.
 * `direct`: If `true`, returns only direct subclasses.
 * `prefixes`: JSON format prefix map.

* **Superclasses (DL Query):** Retrieves superclasses of a class expression.
 `GET /kbs/vfb/superclasses?object={QUERY}&direct=true&includeThing=false&includeDeprecated=true`

* **Equivalent Classes:**
 `GET /kbs/vfb/equivalent?object={QUERY}&direct=true`

* **Satisfiability Check:** Returns a boolean indicating if a class expression is satisfiable.
 `GET /kbs/vfb/satisfiable?object={QUERY}`

* **Instances:** Retrieves individual instances of a class expression.
 `GET /kbs/vfb/instances?object={QUERY}&direct=true`

* **Types:** Retrieves the classes (types) of a named individual.
 `GET /kbs/vfb/types?object={INDIVIDUAL_IRI}&direct=true`

* **SPARQL Query (GET):** Executes a SPARQL query encoded in the URL.
 `GET /kbs/vfb/sparql?query={SPARQL_STRING}`
 * Response format: `application/sparql-results+xml`

* **SPARQL Query (POST):** Executes a SPARQL query contained in the request body.
 `POST /kbs/vfb/sparql`
 * Header: `Content-Type: application/sparql-query`
 * Body: The SPARQL query text.

* **Query Expansion:** Expands Owlet-style embedded class expressions into standard SPARQL filters.
 `GET /kbs/vfb/expand` or `POST /kbs/vfb/expand`

**Common Query Patterns:**
You can use full IRIs (e.g., `[External link removed]`) or short forms (e.g., ``) for identifiers.

* Find all subclasses of a term:
 `GET /kbs/vfb/subclasses?object=&direct=false&includeDeprecated=false&includeEquivalent=true`

* Find neuron classes with parts in a specific region (using relation `RO_0002131` "part of"):
 `GET /kbs/vfb/subclasses?object=<[External link removed]> and <[External link removed]> some {REGION_IRI}&direct=false&includeDeprecated=false&includeEquivalent=true`

* Find neurons with presynaptic terminals in a region (using relation `RO_0002113`):
 `GET /kbs/vfb/subclasses?object=<[External link removed]> and <[External link removed]> some {REGION_IRI}&direct=false&includeDeprecated=false&includeEquivalent=true`

**SPARQL Example:**
To select neurons labeled with "GABA":

```sparql
PREFIX owl: <[External link removed]>
PREFIX rdfs: <[External link removed]>
SELECT?neuron?label
WHERE {
?neuron rdfs:subClassOf <[External link removed]>.
?neuron rdfs:label?label.
 FILTER(CONTAINS(?label, "GABA"))
}
```

**Response Formats:**
Owlery defaults to `application/json`. Other supported formats include `text/plain`, `application/rdf+xml`, and `text/turtle`. These can be specified via the `Accept` header or the `format` query parameter.

For Python-based programmatic access, official documentation is available for the VFB Connect library.

results.title: API: integrations
results.question: How do I explore Virtual Fly Brain neurons using Navis or pymaid?
results.response:
To explore Virtual Fly Brain neurons using `navis`, you can load example neurons or create `NeuronList` objects to analyze properties such as cable length, node count, and soma location. The `navis` library serves as a core Python tool for analyzing these neurons, while `pymaid` functions as a Python client to interface with VFB's CATMAID servers. VFB's documentation does not appear to cover `pymaid` usage details.

You can load example neurons (such as olfactory projection neurons from the hemibrain dataset) and inspect their properties directly:

```python
import navis

# Load one of the example neurons shipped with navis
# (these are olfactory projection neurons from the hemibrain data set)
n = navis.example_neurons(1, kind='skeleton')

# Print some basic info
n

# Access specific properties directly
n.id
n.root
n.nodes.head()

# Reroot neuron to another node
n2 = n.reroot(new_root=2)
n2.root
```

Key properties available for analysis include:
* `bbox`: bounding box of the neuron
* `cable_length`: cable length
* `id`: every neuron has an ID
* `nodes`: the SWC node table underlying the neuron
* `reroot`: reroot neuron
* `plot2d` / `plot3d`: plot the neuron
* `copy`: make and return a copy
* `prune_twigs`: remove small terminal twigs

To work with multiple neurons simultaneously, you can use `NeuronList`, which supports indexing, slicing, and filtering based on neuron properties:

```python
# Get more than one example neuron
nl = navis.example_neurons(5)

# Create a neuron list manually
my_nl = navis.NeuronList(n)

# Access a single neuron from the list
nl[1]

# Select multiple neurons by index
nl[[1, 2]]

# Slice the list
nl[1:3]

# Select neurons by name
nl['754534424']

# Select neurons by ID using the.idx indexer
nl.idx[[754534424, 722817260]]

# Access properties across all neurons in the list (returns numpy arrays)
nl.n_nodes

# Filter neurons by a specific property
nl[nl.n_nodes >= 4500]
```

turns.question: What is the mushroom body?
turns.response:
The [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") is a bilaterally paired neuropil structure situated postero-dorsally in the protocerebrum that functions in olfactory associative learning and memory. It is divided into three main parts: the calyx, which is closest to the cortex and receives sensory interneuron afferents; the pedunculus, a thick axon bundle extending from the calyx to the base of the lobes; and the mushroom body lobe system, which consists of a vertical branch and a medial branch. These structures exhibit different morphologies at different life stages.

The [adult mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003684 "Open adult mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") lobes display a compartmental organisation where the dendrites of mushroom body output neurons and the axon terminals of dopaminergic neurons tile the lobes into a stereotyped grid of 15 compartments.

**Sources:**
* Lee et al., 1999

turns.question: What is the fan-shaped body?
turns.response:
The [fan-shaped body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003679 "Open fan-shaped body in Virtual Fly Brain") is the largest synaptic neuropil domain of the adult central complex, located posterior to the ellipsoid body and anterior to the protocerebral bridge. It is composed of a rough two-dimensional grid of layers and columns. Eight horizontal layers, numbered bottom to top, form a fan shape and can be divided into vertical columns (sometimes called staves, slices, or segments). An additional, much narrower, ninth layer, which lacks a columnar organization, sits dorsal to layer eight. The number of columns varies for different neuronal types.

These anatomical descriptions are supported by literature including Hanesch et al. (1989, 1998), Wolff et al. (2015), Hulse et al. (2021), Ito et al. (2014), and Scheffer et al. (2020).

Its central opening, the ellipsoid body canal, points anteriorly and contains an axon tract known as the anterior bundle. The structure is divided into concentric layers and 16 radial segments (8 per hemisphere), which are numbered 1–8 from superior medial to inferior medial.

turns.response:
A [Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003686 "Open Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain") is an intrinsic neuron of the mushroom body. These cells have tightly-packed cell bodies situated in the rind above the calyx of the mushroom body.

Kenyon cells are a well-studied, functionally central cell class in the fly brain that exhibit high variability between individuals. For instance, they are about 30% more numerous per hemisphere in the FlyWire connectome than in the hemibrain connectome.

VFB holds data on Kenyon cells, including records for subclasses, single-cell RNA sequencing data, transgene expression, and upstream and downstream connectivity classes.

turns.question: What is the mushroom body?
turns.response:
The [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") is a bilaterally paired neuropil structure situated postero-dorsally in the protocerebrum that functions in olfactory associative learning and memory. It is divided into three main parts: the calyx, which is closest to the cortex and receives sensory interneuron afferents; the pedunculus, a thick axon bundle extending from the calyx to the base of the lobes; and the mushroom body lobe system, consisting of a vertical branch and a medial branch that exhibit different structures at different life stages (Lee et al., 1999; Ito et al., 2014; Li et al., 2020).

The [adult mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003684 "Open adult mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") lobes display a compartmental organisation where the dendrites of mushroom body output neurons (MBONs) and the axon terminals of dopaminergic neurons (DANs) tile the lobes into a stereotyped grid of 15 compartments.

**Sources:**
* Lee, T., et al. (1999).
* Ito, K., et al. (2014).
* Li, H., et al. (2020).
* VFB Anatomy Diagrams: Compartmentalization of mushroom body lobes.

turns.question: What is the protocerebral bridge?
turns.response:
The [protocerebral bridge](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003668 "Open protocerebral bridge in Virtual Fly Brain") is a handle bar-shaped synaptic neuropil located just posterior to the fan-shaped body. It forms a dorso-posteriorly located part of the central complex and is embedded in the cortex between the calyces of the two mushroom bodies. Structurally, it consists of a row of 18 connected slices, with 9 on each side of the midline numbered 1 to 9 from medial to lateral. The lateral edge of the protocerebral bridge ends at the posterior end of the inferior clamp near the medial equatorial fascicle.

**Sources:**
* Ito and Awasaki, 2008
* Wolff et al., 2015
* Ito et al., 2014
* Boyan and Williams, 2011
* Hanesch et al., 1989
* VFB Database (VFB)

results.title: Welcome screen — olfactory system overview
results.question: How does the olfactory system work in flies?

status_messages.message: The plan is contested — sampling again before committing.

results.response:
The [olfactory system](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00007688 "Open olfactory system in Virtual Fly Brain") in flies functions as an anatomical network dedicated to the sensory perception of smell. Information flows through a feed-forward circuit that begins at the antenna and proceeds to the antennal lobe, then diverges to the mushroom body and the lateral horn.

This pathway utilizes specific neuron classes to process odor signals:
* **Input:** Antennal-lobe receptor neurons detect odors at the antenna.
* **Local Processing:** Antennal lobe local neurons process signals within the antennal lobe.
* **Relay:** Uniglomerular and multiglomerular projection neurons transmit information from the antennal lobe to higher brain centers.
* **Higher Processing:** In the mushroom body, Kenyon cells receive input, which is modulated by MBONs (mushroom body output neurons) and DANs (dopaminergic neurons). Simultaneously, signals reach the lateral horn via lateral horn neurons and wedge projection neurons.

VFB holds data annotating [315](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00007688,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in olfactory system") neuron types and [368](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00007688,PartsOf "Run in VFB: Parts of olfactory system") subparts associated with the olfactory system.

turns.question: What is the ellipsoid body?
turns.response: The [ellipsoid body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003678 "Open ellipsoid body in Virtual Fly Brain") is a doughnut-shaped synaptic neuropil domain of the central complex of the adult brain that lies just anterior to the fan-shaped body. Its hole, known as the ellipsoid body canal, points anteriorly and contains an axon tract called the anterior bundle. The structure is divided into concentric layers and 16 radial segments (8 per hemisphere), which are numbered 1–8 from superior medial to inferior medial.
